# temps_otel_alert_rule (Resource)

An alert on an OpenTelemetry metric a project sends to Temps, or on the number of log lines matching a saved search. Today only the `static` detector is evaluated.

Import with `<project_id>/<id>`.

Required API key permissions: `otel:read`, `otel:write`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "temps_otel_alert_rule" "checkout_latency" {
  project_id        = temps_project.web.id
  name              = "Slow checkout"
  metric_name       = "http.server.duration"
  aggregation       = "p95"
  detection_config  = jsonencode({ kind = "static", comparator = "gt", threshold = 500 })
  window_secs       = 300
  for_duration_secs = 120
  severity          = "warning"
  label_filters     = jsonencode([["http.route", "/checkout"]])
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `aggregation` (String) How the metric's points in a window are combined. A log alert counts lines: use `count`. One of `avg`, `sum`, `min`, `max`, `count`, `rate`, `p50`, `p90`, `p95`, `p99`.
- `detection_config` (String) The detector, for example `jsonencode({ kind = "static", comparator = "gt", threshold = 500 })`. Comparators: `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`. A JSON document; use `jsonencode(...)`.
- `name` (String) Name of the rule.
- `project_id` (Number) ID of the project.
- `severity` (String) Severity of the alarm. One of `info`, `warning`, `critical`.
- `window_secs` (Number) Length of the window the metric is aggregated over, in seconds.

### Optional

- `dynamic_alerts` (Boolean) With `group_by`, fire one alarm per breaching series instead of one for the aggregate. Unset is `false`.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Evaluate the rule.
- `for_duration_secs` (Number) Seconds the breach must last before the alarm fires; `0` fires at once.
- `group_by` (List of String) Label keys to break the metric down by, at most 2. Unset watches the aggregate.
- `grouped_notification_threshold` (Number) When more series than this start firing at once, only the first notification gets charts, 1-1000. Unset is 5.
- `label_filters` (String) Label equality filters, all of which must match: `jsonencode([["region", "eu"]])`. At most 10. Unset matches every series. A JSON document; use `jsonencode(...)`.
- `max_series` (Number) Most series evaluated with `dynamic_alerts`, 1-100. Unset is 20.
- `metric_name` (String) OpenTelemetry metric watched. Required unless `source` is a saved log search: leave it unset there, Temps names that series `logs.matched_lines`.
- `source` (String) What the rule watches: `jsonencode({ kind = "metric" })` (used when unset) or `jsonencode({ kind = "logs", saved_search_id = 3 })`. A JSON document; use `jsonencode(...)`.

### Read-Only

- `detection_kind` (String) Kind of the detector.
- `id` (String) Import ID, `<project_id>/<id>`.
- `last_state` (String) `ok`, `firing` or `unknown`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <project_id>/<id>
terraform import temps_otel_alert_rule.checkout_latency 8/12
```
